account_number.description: The account number in the source system. This, along with the import_supplier, will be used to find the account in Kraken.

dry_run.description: Whether to run the transactions creation process in dry-run mode. Running in dry-run mode will not create any transactions.

external_account_number.description: The account number in the source system. This, along with the import_supplier, will be used to find the account in Kraken.

import_supplier.description: The import supplier code that the account was imported on to. This, along with the external_account_number, will be used to find the account in Kraken.

x-enum-descriptions.ORIGIN_BUSINESS_NO_CONTRACT: Origin Business - No Contracts e.g. trustee

transactions.description: A list of financial transactions to be imported onto the account.

x-validators.name: Validate that account data is staged and account created
x-validators.description: Validate that an account exists for the external_account_number and import_supplier code. This means that the import data must already have been staged and processed into an account.

x-validators.name: Validate that migration is ongoing
x-validators.description: Validate whether or not an import supplier is open for further data migration.

x-validators.name: Validate unique transaction IDs
x-validators.description: Validate that all transaction IDs provided are unique.

amount.description: The amount of the transaction. e.g. if the customer has a consumption charge worth 23.43, this equates to a transaction of type CHARGE of 23.43. Payments and repayments must be positive numbers. Generally charges and credits are also positive, but may be negative to represent reversed charges or credits, or if an incorrect estimated reading has resulted in a negative consumption charge. Provide this amount in the currency's major unit rather than its minor unit (for example euros rather than cents, or pounds rather than pence). These examples are illustrative only; the same applies to any currency that has a major and minor unit. For currencies without a minor unit, such as the Japanese yen, pass the value as-is.

billing_document_identifier.description: The identifier from the source system that groups a set of transactions together. This will be used in Kraken during the migration of historical statement transactions to create an archived billing document. For now this field is only required if HISTORICAL_STATEMENT_REQUIRE_SINGLE_BILLING_DOCUMENT_IDENTIFIER settings is ON and is meant for only historical_statements_transactions. Passing this to other transactions like current_statement_transactions or transactions_in_open_settlement_period will raise validation error.

display_note.description: The customer-facing note that can be displayed in a statement or email to the customer.

tax_items.description: For SUPPLY_CHARGE and CHARGE transactions only, tax items contain details about the tax. If not provided will be set to default zero tax.

transaction_id.description: The unique internal identifier for the transaction.

end_date.description: The end date for the billing period, inclusive.

external_rate_identifier.description: The external identifier of the rate used to generate the charge for this line item. Only required if Kraken is configured to use placeholder rates when creating supply charge line items.

net_amount.description: Charge amount for the line item. Provide this amount in the currency's major unit rather than its minor unit (for example euros rather than cents, or pounds rather than pence). These examples are illustrative only; the same applies to any currency that has a major and minor unit. For currencies without a minor unit, such as the Japanese yen, pass the value as-is.

network_tariff_distributor_code.description: The distributor code identifying the network tariff library entry. Required when importing a supply charge line item backed by an NTL rate.

network_tariff_rate_code.description: The rate code identifying the specific rate within the network tariff. Must match a READY_TO_BILL rate whose effective period covers the line item period.

network_tariff_tariff_code.description: The tariff code identifying the network tariff library entry. Required when importing a supply charge line item backed by an NTL rate.

number_of_units.description: E.g. cubic meters consumed for the period, days on supply for fixed charges or RV proportion for period for unmetered RV charges.

params.description:
Additional parameters for the line item.

Specify the following keys to control line item charge targets:

  • Supply point charge target:
    • charge_target_type: SUPPLY_POINT
  • Register charge target:
    • charge_target_type: REGISTER
    • charge_target_meter_serial: Serial number for the register's meter
    • charge_target_identifier: Register identifier

x-validators.name: Validate supply charge target
x-validators.description: Validate that the supply charge target are supplied correctly in params.

price_per_unit.description: Price per unit for the line item. If this is not provided, then the price per unit from the relevant product rate will be used instead. Provide this amount in the currency's major unit rather than its minor unit (for example euros rather than cents, or pounds rather than pence). These examples are illustrative only; the same applies to any currency that has a major and minor unit. For currencies without a minor unit, such as the Japanese yen, pass the value as-is.

rate_band.description: Rate of the product this charge is for. Must match an existing rate of a product product_code. Rate must be active from start_date to end_date.

rate_specification_code.description: Rate specification code of the product this charge is for. This code must refer to an existing rate specification within the product.

start_date.description: The start date for the billing period, inclusive.

units.description: For metered accounts only. List of decimal numbers representing the meter readings for the billing period.

x-validators.name: Validate line item units
x-validators.description: Validates that the line item units provided in the payload is a list of two items only.

x-validators.name: Validate ⁨end_date⁩ not before ⁨start_date⁩
x-validators.description: Validates that ⁨end_date⁩, if given, is on or later than ⁨start_date⁩.

x-validators.name: Validate the line item net amount
x-validators.description: Validate that the line item net amount is equal to the price per unit multiplied by the number of units.

x-validators.description: Validate line items include exactly one of rate_band, rate_specification_code, or time_series_specification_code.

x-validators.name: Validates supply charge line item rate
x-validators.description: This validation only applies to transactions of type supply charge. Validates that product code is provided and a product exists with that code. Validates that line items are provided and each line item rate band exists for the product.

x-validators.name: Validate that the given price per unit matches an existing rate price per unit
x-validators.description: Validate that the given price per unit matches an existing rate price per unit. If the existing rate is a dynamic rate (i.e. it has a NaN price per unit), then there must be a price per unit in the payload.

x-validators.name: Validate line item number of units
x-validators.description: Validate that the line item number of units matches the number of days in the period provided for standing charges.

x-validators.name: Validate that the total transaction amount is correct
x-validators.description: Ensure that the total line items amount matches transaction amount.

x-validators.name: Ensure supply point identifier is provided when line items use rate_specification_code
x-validators.description: Validate that supply_point_identifier is provided when any line item contains a rate_specification_code, as the supply point is required for rate resolution.

x-validators.name: Validate that the line items do not overlap with any already charged periods
x-validators.description: Validate that the line item periods do not overlap with any already charged periods for a supply point.
